chapter: Hines 1935-38, Gus Arnheim and Billy Eckstine
title: The state trooper and Earl Hines hiding in the bus
summary: A trooper takes the drunk's side until a white Hollywood fan intervenes, and Hines escapes to hide among the clothes in the bus.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x:
Yeah. I unloosened that thing. I says, look like we goin' die tonight, you know. So this cat went away. In a few minutes he came back, and when he came back, he came back with a state trooper. Now the state trooper was supposed to be there for our protection, everybody's protection, keep any confusion out. The first thing this state trooper said is, when he walked to Earl, he says, 'hey, nigger, what's the matter with you that you can't play this white man's request?'

So Earl says -- Earl still is not with it, you know, like now he's like -- kill me, you know? He says, 'what ar e you talking about?' He says, 'you going to take this drunken bum's word over mine, and I'm sober. I haven't had a drink. This man is drunk. I mean, and we trying to play here. We played 'Honeysuckle Rose.' If you don't recognize Honeysuckle Rose when we're playing it, well then I'm sorry. Tell him to get away from me.'

So this cat said, 'what did you say?' By that time up walked another white fellow. He was very sharp and everything. And he didn't know what was going on. And he walked up to Earl, and he said, 'Earl Hines, baby, how you doin'?' We had -- you know -- and he says, 'hey, you remember we were at Bing Crosby's party?' He says -- at that time they
were building Little Hollywood down in -- between Fort Lauderdale and Miami, like, you know. He says, what do you know, baby, he says, come on over to the table and have a drink with me.

So this cop, this state trooper says, what? I wish you would catch that -- I wish I would catch that nigger goin' over to a table to have a drink at a table in here. So about this time this guy said, what are you talking about? He says, I came to get this gentleman to take him to have a drink. He said, there ain't no niggers gentlemen. And so this guy say, who in the hell do you think you're talking to? And so he went in his inside pocket, and he pulled out a notebook and a pen. He said, what is your name? And he was looking at his badge number, and he was writing. So this shook the state trooper up. See? Well now, he's saying, well, who are you?

He say You see, are you the manager? So this guy said -- no, he didn't get a chance to say anything. Earl said, no, he's not the manager. I'll go get the manager. See? Earl now realizes what we are into, you know? So he's looking for an escape. So Earl said, I'll go get the manager, and he split. Now this left me there. I'm the strawboss. Right? I got to finish up the dance. I got about an hour to go. You know -- did you think that echo was hurtin' us?

Anyway, I got about an hour to go, and I'm saying, now this cat has left me here to be putting up with these people. You know? So when he split, you know, then I mean I'm watching Earl exit, and so I don't know what happened to the guy and the trooper because I've got my eye on Earl. I'm very concerned over Earl. I don't want nothing to happen to him going out the door. I'm ready to go down with him, you know?

Anyway, Earl gets out. I finish up the dance. When we finish up the dance, I go out to the bus, and I'm looking for Earl Hines. And, you know, like we were like a traveling motel then. I mean all of our clothes were hanging up in the back on special racks they put in the bus and everything. And we undress in here -- we undress and dressed in the bus. You know, we traveled so many miles, we didn't have no chance to get any rooms. So I went back there to part the clothes to hang up my uniform, and I looked back there, and there's Earl Hines all back up in these clothes.

And I said, 'man, I said, if you -- look, you going to get me killed,' I said, 'and if you do that, I'm going to get up, and I mean you and I going to fight like mad.' Isn't that something? I'm going to get killed and get up.
But, you know, I thought this was -- to show you like what was happening in the South at that time.
